questions.text: A hospital receives a survey finding that its infection control documentation is incomplete. The FIRST step in responding is to:

options.a: Immediately dispute the finding with the accreditation body
options.b: Perform a root cause analysis to understand why documentation is incomplete and develop a corrective plan
options.c: Reassign the infection control staff to other duties
options.d: Wait until the next survey cycle to address the deficiency

questions.explanation: Understanding the root cause enables development of an effective Plan of Correction that addresses the actual problem rather than just the symptom.

questions.text: Under HIPAA, which of the following is a permissible use of patient information WITHOUT specific patient authorization?

options.a: Sharing patient information with an employer for employment decisions
options.b: Using patient information for treatment, payment, and healthcare operations
options.c: Disclosing patient information to a marketing company
options.d: Providing patient records to a family member without patient consent

questions.explanation: HIPAA permits use of PHI for treatment, payment, and healthcare operations (TPO) without specific patient authorization.

questions.text: A hospital's quality department identifies that its falls prevention protocol does not meet current Joint Commission standards. Which action is MOST appropriate?

options.a: Continue using the current protocol until the next survey
options.b: Revise the protocol to meet the standard, implement it, and verify compliance through monitoring
options.c: Request a waiver from The Joint Commission
options.d: Document the gap and refer it to the medical staff office

questions.explanation: When a gap is identified, the correct response is to update the practice to meet the standard, implement the change, and monitor compliance.

questions.text: Which of the following is a CMS 'never event' (Serious Reportable Event)?

options.a: A patient acquiring a minor skin tear during repositioning
options.b: Surgery performed on the wrong patient
options.c: A medication dose being administered 30 minutes late
options.d: A patient experiencing a headache after a lumbar puncture

questions.explanation: Wrong-patient surgery is a CMS Serious Reportable Event (never event) — a preventable error that should never occur if proper safeguards are in place.

questions.text: A quality professional is preparing a regulatory compliance report. Which of the following BEST demonstrates ongoing survey readiness?

options.a: Data showing compliance metrics are consistently monitored and trending toward improvement
options.b: Evidence that staff completed training modules the week before the survey
options.c: A list of temporary measures implemented specifically for the survey
options.d: Testimonials from staff that they feel ready for the survey

questions.explanation: Consistently monitored and improving compliance data demonstrates a culture of continuous readiness, not just pre-survey preparation.

questions.text: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of the Joint Commission's ORYX initiative?

options.a: To provide a voluntary peer networking program for hospital CEOs
options.b: To integrate performance measurement data into the accreditation process
options.c: To standardize physician credentialing across states

questions.explanation: The ORYX initiative requires accredited organizations to collect and submit standardized performance measurement data, integrating it into TJC's accreditation process.

questions.text: A hospital is notified of an unannounced CMS survey. How should the quality team respond?

options.a: Request a 24-hour postponement to prepare staff
options.b: Welcome the surveyors and provide requested access and documentation
options.c: Alert only senior leadership and restrict surveyor access until preparation is complete
options.d: Contact legal counsel before allowing surveyors to enter

questions.explanation: Organizations with true continuous readiness should welcome unannounced surveys. Obstructing access or delaying entry may constitute non-compliance.

questions.text: Which regulatory body enforces workplace safety standards in healthcare settings?
questions.explanation: OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Administration) enforces workplace safety and health regulations, including bloodborne pathogen standards for healthcare settings.

questions.text: A hospital's compliance program identifies a pattern of upcoding in billing practices. The MOST appropriate next step is to:

options.a: Continue the practice and consult legal counsel only if audited
options.b: Voluntarily report the issue through the OIG Self-Disclosure Protocol and take corrective action
options.c: Quietly stop the practice without reporting
options.d: Wait to see if CMS identifies the issue during a routine audit

questions.explanation: The OIG Self-Disclosure Protocol allows organizations to voluntarily report potential fraud violations, which generally results in more favorable resolution than waiting for detection.

questions.text: Which of the following is the PRIMARY benefit of healthcare accreditation for patients?

options.b: Accreditation provides assurance that the organization meets established quality and safety standards
options.c: Accreditation reduces the cost of care for patients
options.d: Accreditation ensures all staff are nationally certified

questions.explanation: Accreditation gives patients confidence that an organization has met recognized quality and safety standards through rigorous external evaluation.
